sections.title: Basic Config — every setting
sections.excerpt: Basic Config — every setting | Screen-level behaviour: entrance animations, cached media, a device-permission prompt, and auto-advance. This guide documents every setting of the Basic Config block, grouped by area. Each setting matches a real control in the screen editor.

sections.title: Play Screen Animations
sections.excerpt: Play Screen Animations | Turns on the entrance, exit, and element animations you set up in the screen's animation settings; when off, the screen simply appears instantly. Use it on intro and hero screens where motion feels polished and guides the eye. Leave it off on dense question screens where visitors want the controls ready to tap right away.

sections.title: Auto-Advance After A Delay
sections.excerpt: Auto-Advance After A Delay | When on, the screen moves to the next step on its own after the countdown you set below, with a visible timer. Off by default. Great for splash or 'analyzing...' screens, but never use it where visitors must tap or answer, like questions or your paywall, or you'll skip them past the response or sale.

sections.title: Auto-Advance Duration
sections.excerpt: Auto-Advance Duration | The number of seconds or minutes (unit chosen below) before the screen moves on by itself, from 1 to 300. Only used when auto-advance is on. Keep it short, about 2 to 4 seconds for a splash or 'analyzing...' screen, so visitors aren't left waiting and bouncing.

sections.title: Seconds Or Minutes
sections.excerpt: Seconds Or Minutes | Sets whether the auto-advance duration above counts in seconds or minutes. Only shows when auto-advance is on. Seconds is the right choice for nearly every onboarding screen; minutes is rarely useful and risks visitors leaving before the screen ever advances.

sections.title: Reuse cached media
sections.excerpt: Reuse cached media | When on, the screen reuses media it has already cached instead of re-downloading it, which can speed up loading for visitors on slow or flaky connections. Leave it off by default for standard web ad funnels, since there's nothing to reuse until assets are cached. Turn it on only if you ship pre-bundled assets or expect a lot of poor-connectivity traffic.

sections.title: Ask For A Device Permission
sections.excerpt: Ask For A Device Permission | When on, this screen pops the phone's own permission request, notifications, location, or ad tracking, chosen in the field below, as it appears. This fires in the native app SDK, not on a plain web page. Put it on a screen that first explains why you need it so far more people tap Allow.

sections.title: Which Permission To Ask For
sections.excerpt: Which Permission To Ask For | Picks which device permission this screen requests: push notifications, ad tracking (needed for accurate ad attribution on iPhones), or location. Only shows when the permission request is turned on. Choose what your funnel truly needs, ad tracking if you rely on ad-network attribution, notifications for re-engaging users later.
